title: Multiple India-based CCTV Cameras (Update A)
overview: Affected Products Multiple India-based CCTV Cameras Vendor: D-Link (India Limited), Sparsh Securitech, Securus CCTV Product Version: D-Link (India Limited) DCS-F5614-L1: <=v1.03.038, Securus CCTV Purple Series: <15-12-2025, Sparsh Securitech IP CCTV Cameras: vers:all/* Product Status: known_affected Remediations None available Sparsh Securitech did not respond to CISA's requests for coordination. Users of cameras from this vendor are encouraged to reach out to their respective customer service representatives to see if their specific model of camera is affected. None available Sparsh Securitech: info@sparshsecuritech.com or use the form at https://www.sparshsecuritech.com/contact-us None available Sparsh Securitech: info@sparshsecuritech.com or use the form at https://www.sparshsecuritech.com/contact-us Mitigation D-Link has released a security advisory and a software update for the affected camera model. Please visit this D-Link Security Announcement at https://supportannouncement.us.dlink.com/security/publication.aspx?name=SAP10462 for further information. Vendor fix D-Link strongly urges all users to install the relevant updates and regularly check for further updates. After downloading the software update, it is essential to ALWAYS validate its success by comparing the software version on your product interface to the software update version. Vendor fix Securus has released a software update for the affected camera model. Please visit the Purple Series Product Information Page at https://www.securuscctv.com/hd-cameras/purple-series for further information. Mitigation Securus CCTV: sales@securuscctv.com or use the form at https://www.securuscctv.com/contactus Mitigation Securus CCTV: sales@securuscctv.com or use the form at https://www.securuscctv.com/contactus Vendor fix Securus recommends all users update to the firmware package dated 15-12-2025. Mitigation The models listed in this advisory are known only for D-Link India Limited and Securus. Users of cameras produced by the other listed vendors are encouraged to evaluate this vulnerability within their environment. Relevant CWE: CWE-306 Missing Authentication for Critical Function Metrics CVSS Version Base Score Base Severity Vector String 3.1 9.4 CRITICAL CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:L Acknowledgments Souvik Kandar reported this vulnerability to CISA Legal Notice and Terms of Use This product is provided subject to this Notification (https://www.cisa.gov/notification) and this Privacy & Use policy (https://www.cisa.gov/privacy-policy). Recommended Practices CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability, such as: Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the Internet. Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks. When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices. CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures. CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies. CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets. Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies. Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents. No known public exploitation specifically targeting this vulnerability has been reported to CISA at this time.
